2607.14006.title: Rethinking Penetration Testing for AI-Enabled Systems: From Resource Compromise to Behavioral Objective Violation
2607.14006.paper_summary: Penetration testing traditionally evaluates whether adversaries can exploit weaknesses in software, infrastructure, configurations, or operational controls to achieve security-relevant compromise. This paradigm remains necessary for AI-enabled systems, but it is no longer sufficient. In such systems, adversaries may influence prompts, retrieved content, sensor inputs, training data, memory, tools, or human-AI interaction loops to alter system behavior without directly compromising the underlying infrastructure. This paper reframes penetration testing for AI-enabled systems as objective-driven behavioral evaluation. We define an AI-enabled system as one in which learned models materially influence behavior affecting operational outcomes, and we define AI-enabled penetration as the feasible induction of AI-governed behavior that violates one or more operational objectives under an explicit threat model. This definition preserves conventional penetration testing while extending it to adversarial pathways such as prompt injection, indirect prompt injection, data poisoning, sensor manipulation, retrieval poisoning, tool misuse, and agentic misalignment. We further propose a testing workflow that identifies operational objectives, maps AI-governed behavior, analyzes adversarial influence surfaces, defines behavioral failure criteria, executes scenario-based tests, and reports evidence linking adversarial action to objective violation. A running example involving an AI-enabled security operations center assistant illustrates how penetration may occur through behavioral influence rather than infrastructure compromise. Together, the definitions, workflow, and example provide a technical framework for evaluating adversarial success in deployed AI-enabled systems.
2607.14006.paper_summary_zh: 滲透測試傳統上評估對手是否可以利用軟體、基礎設施、配置或操作控制中的弱點來達成與安全相關的妥協。這種範式對於AI驅動的系統仍然是必要的，但已不再足夠。在這些系統中，對手可能會影響提示、檢索內容、感測器輸入、訓練數據、記憶體、工具或人機互動循環，以在不直接妥協基礎設施的情況下改變系統行為。本文將AI驅動系統的滲透測試重新框架為以目標為驅動的行為評估。我們將AI驅動系統定義為學習模型在影響操作結果的行為上具有實質性影響的系統，並將AI驅動的滲透定義為在明確的威脅模型下，誘導違反一個或多個操作目標的AI治理行為的可行性。這一定義保留了傳統的滲透測試，同時將其擴展到對抗性路徑，如提示注入、間接提示注入、數據中毒、感測器操控、檢索中毒、工具誤用和代理不對齊。我們進一步提出了一個測試工作流程，該流程識別操作目標、映射AI治理行為、分析對抗性影響面、定義行為失敗標準、執行基於場景的測試，並報告將對抗行動與目標違反聯繫起來的證據。一個涉及AI驅動的安全運營中心助手的運行範例說明了如何通過行為影響而非基礎設施妥協來發生滲透。這些定義、工作流程和範例共同提供了一個技術框架，用於評估已部署的AI驅動系統中的對抗性成功。
